title: Transitions & signal words Practice 2
description: 4 short texts - 8 focused transitions & signal words questions
subject: rla
passage:
TEXT A - Clinic Hours

The clinic opened one evening each week. appointments became available to more patients who work during the day.

TEXT B - Trail Signs

The park replaced several faded trail signs. one new sign includes a map showing the distance to the lake.

TEXT C - Workshop Seats

The repair workshop is free. registration is required because only twenty workbenches are available.

TEXT D - Water Test

Researchers measured water temperature at five sites. they recorded dissolved oxygen and stream depth at the same locations.

questions.prompt: Which transition best connects these ideas? "The clinic opened one evening each week. _____, appointments became available to more patients who work during the day."
questions.explanation: Evening hours make appointments available to more daytime workers, so the second sentence states a result.
questions.rule: Name the relationship first, then prove it with the surrounding text.

options.whyWrong: The second idea is a benefit produced by the first, not a contrast.
The second sentence gives an outcome, not an example of opening hours.
Meanwhile signals simultaneous timing and misses the causal relationship.

questions.prompt: What relationship should the transition signal?
questions.explanation: Expanded appointment access follows from opening during the evening.
questions.rule: Name the relationship first, then prove it with the surrounding text.

options.whyWrong: The second idea does not oppose the first.
It describes the consequence of the schedule change.
The relationship is stronger than simple addition because one change leads to the other.

questions.prompt: Which transition best connects these ideas? "The park replaced several faded trail signs. _____, one new sign includes a map showing the distance to the lake."
questions.explanation: The map is one specific example of the new replacement signs.
questions.rule: Name the relationship first, then prove it with the surrounding text.

options.whyWrong: The sentences do not contrast.
The map is not presented as a consequence caused by replacing faded signs.
No opposing idea is introduced.

questions.prompt: What relationship should the transition signal?
questions.explanation: The second sentence gives a particular instance of the broader statement about new signs.
questions.rule: Name the relationship first, then prove it with the surrounding text.

options.whyWrong: The map is not an effect of the first sentence in the logical sense being tested.
The example supports the first idea rather than qualifying it.
It is related as a specific instance, not merely another independent fact.

questions.prompt: Which transition best connects these ideas? "The repair workshop is free. _____, registration is required because only twenty workbenches are available."
questions.explanation: The workshop being free sounds broadly accessible, but required registration limits access because space is scarce.
questions.rule: Name the relationship first, then prove it with the surrounding text.

options.whyWrong: Registration is explained by limited benches, not as a result of the workshop being free.
The registration rule is a qualification, not an example of free admission.
The two ideas are not similar; the second limits the first.

questions.prompt: What relationship should the transition signal?
questions.explanation: The registration requirement qualifies the benefit of a free workshop.
questions.rule: Name the relationship first, then prove it with the surrounding text.

options.whyWrong: The qualification is not caused by the workshop being free.
It does not illustrate what free means.
Simple addition misses the limitation created by scarce workbenches.

questions.prompt: Which transition best connects these ideas? "Researchers measured water temperature at five sites. _____, they recorded dissolved oxygen and stream depth at the same locations."
questions.explanation: The researchers recorded oxygen and depth as extra measurements at the same sites.
questions.rule: Name the relationship first, then prove it with the surrounding text.

options.whyWrong: No contrast is present.
Temperature measurement did not cause the team to record the other variables.
Oxygen and depth are additional measurements, not examples of water temperature.

questions.prompt: What relationship should the transition signal?
questions.explanation: The second sentence adds measurements collected alongside temperature.
questions.rule: Name the relationship first, then prove it with the surrounding text.

options.whyWrong: The variables are not presented as opposing information.
One measurement is not caused by the other.
Oxygen and depth are separate variables, not examples of temperature.

curriculum.learningObjective: Apply transitions & signal words reasoning across varied original texts and explain answers from textual evidence.
